last_assistant_message:
**[Rigby]: All three bugs fixed and independently verified. One thing I did not touch — read to the end.**

**1. `infer_session_id()` — fixed in both copies.** `hook_utils.py` and `eval-agent-start.py` now key off `index[-1].get("started", "")` instead of the nonexistent `"id"` field. Confirmed against the real schema — 42 real records on disk, none have ever had an `id` field, all have `started`. No schema migration, no new field, exactly as directed. Both files compile clean.

**2. `detect_workflow()` tightened.** Now requires an explicit path reference, a slash command, or a run-verb (run/start/kick off/execute/launch/invoke/fire off/fire up/begin) within 3 words of the workflow name/slug, either order. I unit-tested it against 11 cases including the exact failure class that produced LE19LT ("we discussed boot instrumentation earlier tonight, the eval record for boot never fired" → no match) plus positive cases ("run boot", "/boot", "kick off shutdown cleanup", "please run the weekly review workflow now") — all 11 pass. One false-positive I caught myself in testing ("what does boot even do" was matching because I'd included "do" as a run-verb) — removed "do" from the verb list before it shipped.

**3. `workflow-start.py` retired**, not patched. Removed its `PostToolUse` registration from `.claude/settings.json` (verified still-valid JSON after edit). Left the file on disk with a deprecation header explaining why and pointing at the two mechanisms that supersede it (`eval-agent-start/stop.py` for spawned-subagent workflows, `eval-turn-start/stop.py` for the three `agent: master` workflows) — didn't delete it, for blame/history.

**4. Cleaned up the three contaminated records**, confirming each before removal:
- `eval-20260826T193828-LE19LT.json` — deleted. Spurious boot record: empty `session_id` (bug #1) opened by a bare mention of "boot" in conversation (bug #2), with the unrelated `LZA3KU` incident misattributed into it as a boot failure.
- `eval-20260826T191055-75A708.json` and `eval-20260826T194142-QZAPOH.json` — deleted. Orphaned `plaud-ingest` stubs from the now-retired `workflow-start.py`, permanently stuck `status: in-progress` with no close-out path.

**What I did not do, and why:** mid-review, `workflows/boot/state.yaml`, `workflows/plaud-ingest/state.yaml`, `data/calendar-unified.json`, and `memory/sessions/index.json` changed again — after my earlier revert to committed state. This isn't residue from my own edits (I only touched hook/settings files this pass). The new `plaud-ingest/state.yaml` shows a fresh session `pi-20260826-003` whose own `dedup-method` field narrates my earlier git-revert by name. Something is still actively writing to these files, independent of this conversation's tool calls, and I have no way from here to tell whether that's a real concurrent boot/Knox run happening for real right now versus more of the same unscoped background activity that caused the original incident. Given `err-20260826T193944-LZA3KU` already asserts (unverified by me) that my last revert destroyed legitimate work, I'm not repeating that action a third time on guesswork. I'm leaving all four files exactly as they currently sit and escalating rather than deciding — you have visibility into whether there's a real live session running against this repo right now that I don't.

I also still can't independently confirm `LZA3KU`'s central claim. It cites `QQMBTP` — an entry I already flagged as unverified — as grounds for saying the plaud-ingest backlog I restored was garbage and the version I reverted away from was a legitimate fix. I haven't acted on that claim either way; it needs a real check (ask Knox to re-run discovery cleanly, or check the vault directly) rather than trusting a self-authored file's narrative, same principle I applied to `RJK2JY`.

Nothing committed. All hook files compile; `settings.json` is valid JSON. Recommend you check whether something is still live against this repo before I (or anyone) touches those four files again.
